messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> HIGH: gpu-node-42 kernel panic + kubelet NotReady (auto-page)
pagerduty: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456 — triggered by node-exporter / node-health
ryan_oncall: Acked. I'm on this. Pulling serial console and kube events now. :eyes:
maya_sre: thx. FYI this node hosts a few long-running training pods (team: vision). Might be customer-impact.
ryan_oncall: serial shows: kernel BUG at nvme.c:2234, stack trace... reboot loop. attaching last few lines:
```
[  102.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 2048: GPU HANG
[  102.346789] kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[  105.000001] Rebooting in 10 seconds...
```
eli_engops: kubelet reports NotReady and coredump upload attempted. CSI detach is stuck on a few PVs: "detach timeout".
ryan_oncall: trying `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` but eviction is stalling because of PVC detach.
joel_infra: if disk detach stuck that can block pod eviction; we had a flakey NVMe firmware version on this rack last month. Node is in rack r-07.
ryan_oncall: running runbook step 3 -> requesting serial console IPMI reset now. ipmi command:
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.4.7.123 -U admin -P **** chassis power reset
```
anna_custsuccess: pinging Vision team and a customer contact (acme-ai) to warn of possible training interruption.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by ryan_oncall at 3601234575
ryan_oncall: IPMI reset completed; node came back briefly but kubelet still NotReady, and NVMe partitions remounted readonly. Logs show repeated I/O errors.
maya_sre: can we migrate affected pods to other GPUs? What about preemptible capacity in the dedicated pool?
eli_engops: we can try fallback to dedicated-gpu-pool via pod disruption budget override. I'll trigger eviction from our side for the highest-priority pods.
ryan_oncall: invoking eviction script for training-job-* (lower-priority):
```
for p in $(kubectl get pods -n vision -l app=training -o name); do kubectl delete $p --namespace=vision; done
```
ryan_oncall: some pods fail to terminate due to PVC detach errors: `error: pod has unmounted volumes; waiting` — looks like CSI driver not responding to detach calls.
joel_infra: escalated to hardware RMA queue — filing RMA for host 10.4.7.123. Likely NVMe failure. RMA ticket #RMA-7892
anna_custsuccess: ACME support notified. They're seeing 502s for checkpoint upload endpoints (vision-training). Provided ETA: immediate mitigation attempt, potential 2h impact.
maya_sre: temporary mitigation: create routing rule to avoid scheduling to rack r-07 and enable cache fallback for checkpoint uploads. I'll push a router rule now.
ryan_oncall: applied `nodeAffinity` anti-affinity for new pods to avoid r-07; also updated autoscaler to spin up 2 extra nodes in dedicated-gpu-pool. Watching scheduler logs.
eli_engops: autoscaler is provisioning two nodes in dedicated-gpu-pool (expected ~6 mins). Meanwhile, kicked restart of csi controller on control plane to clear stuck detaches:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/csi-controller
```
pagerduty: Escalation: infra-lead joel_infra notified at 3601234650
joel_infra: seeing NVMe CTL errors in host logs; RMA approved. Recommend migrating any remaining critical pods off gpu-node-42 and marking host unschedulable.
ryan_oncall: marked node unschedulable and added taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-42 node.kubernetes.io/unavailable:NoSchedule` — remaining pending pods moved.
anna_custsuccess: updated ACME and internal slack channel with current status and mitigation steps. Customer asked for postmortem when resolved.
maya_sre: scheduler is now placing new pods on dedicated pool nodes; 3 vision training pods restarted successfully on new nodes. Checkpoint uploads showing recovered throughput.
ryan_oncall: tracking metrics: failed requests peaked at ~18/min during initial failure, now back to baseline ~1/min. Logging incident to incident tracker.
eli_engops: still seeing one PV stuck in Attach state for ~20m. If CSI restart doesn't help we'll need to manually delete attachment object in k8s API as last resort.
joel_infra: RMA tech scheduled for on-site swap in ~4h. Will follow-up with serial logs and hardware swap notes.
ryan_oncall: plan: 1) keep node cordoned + tainted, 2) complete pod migrations, 3) monitor until RMA completes, 4) postmortem and firmware roll for rack r-07. Assigning postmortem owner: maya_sre.
maya_sre: noted. I'll start the postmortem doc and include action items: NVMe firmware upgrade, improve CSI detach retries, add runbook step for manual attachment cleanup.
anna_custsuccess: sent customer follow-up with mitigation summary and estimated timeline. Will loop back when RMA is complete.
ryan_oncall: closing alert in PagerDuty (manual close) — marking incident as mitigated; continuing watch for 1 hour.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident status: Resolved by ryan_oncall at 3601234867
joel_infra: leaving a note to infra runbook: consider replacing NVMe vendor X drives in rack r-07 after RMA results.
eli_engops: will follow up on CSI detach fix in next sprint. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
anna_custsuccess: thanks team, good coordination. I'll capture customer feedback in postmortem.
